user.title: Choose your Huawei scale
user.description: The scale only shows up while someone is standing on it. Step on it now and reopen this dialog if it is not listed, or type its Bluetooth address (AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF). {recognised} recognised device(s) found.

profile.title: Your profile
profile.description: The scale needs your sex, age and height before it can measure, and the integration uses them to calculate body composition. The starting weight is only used until the first measurement.

data_description.birth_date: Type it as YYYY-MM-DD (1985-03-27) or DD/MM/YYYY (27/03/1985).

settings.title: Behaviour and model
settings.description:
Detected model: {model} (from {source}). History import fires an event for measurements stored on the scale that were taken while Home Assistant could not hear it. Frame capture keeps the raw BLE traffic so an unrecognised firmware can be diagnosed: weigh in once, then download the diagnostics or call huawei_scale_pro.dump_frames. Gender encoding and impedance units only need changing if the scale rejects the profile or the body-composition numbers are clearly wrong.

Recognising the person by weight reassigns a weigh-in to the profile whose recent weights match — useful when more than one person uses the scale. The first weigh-in of each person must be done with the right profile selected: the scale needs the profile before it measures, so it cannot be chosen from the weight it has not measured yet. After that the selection follows the person automatically.

A weight that matches nobody within the tolerance is treated as a one-off guest weigh-in: it does not overwrite anyone's sensors and is not used to recognise people later. If the same unusual weight repeats, it is taken as a real change of the selected person's weight and their history is restarted.

data.read_history: Read stored measurements from the scale
data.gender_encoding: Gender encoding in the user profile
data.prefer_scale_body_fat: Huawei Health formulas: take the body fat from the scale and split the rest into water, protein and mineral (recommended). Turn off to compute everything from the impedance with the openScale model.
data.user_match_tolerance_kg: How far the weight may deviate

data_description.birth_date: Type it as YYYY-MM-DD (1985-03-27) or DD/MM/YYYY (27/03/1985).

guest.title: Guest and guest data
guest.description:
A guest is a mode, not a person: their weigh-in goes to no profile, is never used to recognise people by weight, and lives only on the "Guest data" device. Pick it in the "Who is weighing" list next to the profiles.

The scale needs height, age and sex before it measures, and nobody knows a visitor's. Leave the fields blank and the height is guessed from the guest's weight and the age from the resulting BMI — enough for the scale to report a composition. Anything typed here wins over the guess.

data_description.guest_aftermath: "Keep the data" leaves the guest reading on its own sensors and the scale keeps working as usual. "Wait for a person" stops weighing altogether until a person is selected, so repeat guest weigh-ins cannot overwrite the guest sensors and nobody's data is touched.
data_description.guest_height_cm: Blank: the height is derived from the weight.
data_description.guest_age: Blank: the age is derived from height and weight.
